column1: hobble§A stone in the boot hobbled him for the last nine miles, and he finished the walk four hours late.§靴子里的一块石头**使他一瘸一拐**地走完最后九英里，他晚了四小时才走完全程。§
hodgepodge§The regulations are a hodgepodge of four eras, and three of them contradict each other on the same page.§这些规章是四个年代的**大杂烩**，其中三个在同一页上互相矛盾。§
hog§One department hogged nine tenths of the computing time, and the rest of the faculty queued overnight for the rest.§一个系**霸占**了十分之九的机时，其余教员通宵排队争剩下的部分。§
holistic§The holistic approach failed here for a simple reason: nobody was responsible for any particular part of it.§**整体式的**做法在这里失败，原因很简单——没有人对其中任何一部分负责。§holo（全部）
hospitable§The valley is hospitable for four months and, for the other eight, entirely uninhabitable.§这条河谷有四个月**宜居**，其余八个月完全无法居住。§hospit（客人／主人，同 hospital 医院）
hospitality§Their hospitality was overwhelming and impossible to refuse, and we stayed three days longer than planned.§他们的**款待**令人招架不住又无法推辞，我们比计划多住了三天。§
hostility§The hostility was mutual and unspoken, and it shaped every committee decision for nine years.§这种**敌意**是相互而不宣于口的，它塑造了九年间每一项委员会决定。§host（敌人，同 hostile 敌对的）
hubris§Hubris, not incompetence, sank the project: they refused the review that would have caught the flaw.§击沉这个项目的是**狂妄**而非无能——他们拒绝了本能发现缺陷的评审。§
humane§The most humane option was also the cheapest, and it still took the council four years to adopt it.§最**人道的**选项也是最便宜的，议会仍然花了四年才采纳。§human（人）
humility§Her humility was not modesty but method: she assumed she was wrong until the data said otherwise.§她的**谦逊**不是谦虚而是方法——在数据说话之前她假定自己是错的。§humil（低，同 humble 谦卑的）
hybrid§The hybrid outperformed both parent varieties and turned out to be sterile, which nobody had planned for.§这个**杂交种**表现优于两个亲本品种，却是不育的，这是无人预料的。§
hypothetical§The question was hypothetical when he asked it in March and entirely practical by the end of May.§三月他提这个问题时它还是**假设性的**，到五月底已完全是现实问题。§hypo（在下）+ thes（放置，同 thesis 论点）
hysterical§The reaction was hysterical in the press and remarkably calm among the people actually affected.§媒体的反应**歇斯底里**，而真正受影响的人群异常平静。§
icon§The chair became an icon of the period, and the designer earned about nine hundred pounds from it.§这把椅子成了那个时代的**标志**，而设计者从中赚了约九百英镑。§
iconoclast§The iconoclast who attacked the field's central assumption is now the author of its standard textbook.§那位攻击该领域核心假设的**破旧立新者**，如今是它标准教科书的作者。§icon（偶像）+ clast（打碎）
iconoclastic§Her iconoclastic reading of the poem was rejected for two decades and is now taught as the obvious one.§她对这首诗**离经叛道的**解读被否定了二十年，如今被当作显而易见的读法来教。§
idealist§The idealist in the room drafted the clause, and the lawyers spent nine months making it enforceable.§屋里那位**理想主义者**起草了这条条款，律师们花九个月让它变得可执行。§
idealize§We idealize the period because the letters that survive were written by the four people who were happy.§我们**理想化**那个时代，是因为存世的信件出自那四个过得开心的人之手。§
ideologue§The ideologue could not concede a single point, and the negotiation ended where it had begun.§这位**意识形态论者**一步也不肯让，谈判结束时回到了起点。§idea（观念）+ log（说，同 dialogue 对话）
idiosyncratic§His filing system was idiosyncratic and flawless, and nobody has been able to use it since he retired.§他的归档系统**独树一帜**而滴水不漏，自他退休后没人用得了。§idio（自己的，同 idiom 习语）+ syn-（一起）+ cras（混合）
ignominy§The ignominy of the retraction was worse than the error, and he never published in the field again.§撤稿的**耻辱**比错误本身更难受，他再没在这个领域发表过文章。§i-（无）+ gnomin ← nomen（名字，同 nominate 提名）→ 名声没了
illegible§The prescription was illegible, the pharmacist guessed, and the guess put a child in hospital for nine days.§处方**难以辨认**，药剂师猜了一下，这一猜让一个孩子住院九天。§il-（不）+ leg（读，同 legible 易读的）
illicit§The illicit trade is worth more than the legal one, and every attempt to police it has raised the price.§**非法**交易的规模超过合法交易，每一次管制尝试都抬高了价格。§il-（不）+ licit（允许，同 license 许可）
illuminate§One footnote illuminates the whole argument by naming the source the author had spent four chapters concealing.§一条脚注**照亮**了整个论证，因为它点出了作者用四章隐藏的来源。§il-（进入）+ lumin（光，同 luminous 发光的）
illusory§The consensus was illusory: everyone agreed on the words and meant four different things by them.§这种共识是**虚幻的**——人人同意那些字眼，而所指的是四种不同的东西。§il-（进入）+ lud（玩，同 illusion 幻觉）
imaginative§The most imaginative solution came from the maintenance crew, who had never been asked before.§最**富想象力的**方案来自维修班组，而此前从没有人问过他们。§imagin（想象）
imbecile§Calling the plan imbecile was unhelpful and, as four independent reviews later confirmed, broadly accurate.§把这个计划称作**愚蠢**无济于事，而正如四次独立评审后来确认的，大体准确。§
imbue§Nine years in that laboratory imbued her with a suspicion of tidy results that never left her.§在那间实验室的九年**使她浸染**了对漂亮结果的怀疑，此后再未消退。§im-（进入）+ bu（浸泡）
imitation§The imitation is better made than the original and worth about a fortieth as much.§这件**仿制品**做工胜过原件，价值却只有约四十分之一。§imit（模仿，同 image 形象）
immaterial§Whether he intended it is immaterial: the rule turns entirely on what actually happened.§他是否有意是**无关紧要的**——这条规则完全取决于实际发生了什么。§im-（不）+ material（物质的／重要的）
immature§The technology was immature in 1998 and shipped anyway, and the company never recovered from the reviews.§这项技术在 1998 年还**不成熟**却仍然出货，公司再没从那些评测中缓过来。§im-（不）+ mature（成熟）
immersion§Six weeks of immersion taught her more of the language than four years of classes had.§六周的**沉浸**让她学到的语言超过四年课堂所学。§im-（进入）+ mers（浸，同 submerge 淹没）
immobile§The patient stayed immobile for eleven days, and the muscle loss took nine months to reverse.§病人**不能活动**了十一天，肌肉流失花了九个月才逆转。§im-（不）+ mob（移动，同 mobile 移动的）
immobility§The immobility of the market surprised everyone: nine months without a single transaction on the whole street.§市场的**凝滞**让所有人意外——整条街九个月没有一笔交易。§
immoderate§His immoderate praise for one candidate made the panel's other three recommendations look like afterthoughts.§他对某位候选人**过分的**赞美，让评审组另外三项推荐显得像是临时补上的。§im-（不）+ moderate（适度的）
immoral§The practice was legal and immoral, and it took a change in public opinion rather than in law to end it.§这种做法合法而**不道德**，终结它的是舆论而非法律的改变。§
immorality§Charges of immorality were used to remove four officials whose real offence was disagreeing with the mayor.§**不道德**的指控被用来罢免四名官员，而他们真正的罪过是不同意市长。§
immutable§The rules were treated as immutable for sixty years and rewritten, in the end, in a single afternoon.§这些规则被当作**不可更改的**长达六十年，最后在一个下午就重写完了。§im-（不）+ mut（改变，同 mutation 突变）
impartial§An impartial chair would have stopped him at four minutes, and this one let him speak for forty.§一位**公正的**主席会在四分钟时叫停他，而这位让他讲了四十分钟。§im-（不）+ part（部分／偏袒）→ 不偏向哪一边
impasse§Negotiations reached an impasse over a sum that was less than the cost of the negotiations themselves.§谈判因一笔比谈判本身花费还少的金额陷入**僵局**。§im-（不）+ pass（通过）→ 走不过去
impassioned§Her impassioned defense changed four votes, which was three more than anyone had thought possible.§她**慷慨激昂的**辩护改变了四张票，比任何人认为可能的多出三张。§
impassive§His impassive face gave the room nothing, and the verdict was read to complete silence.§他**面无表情**的脸什么也没透露，判决在一片死寂中宣读。§im-（不）+ passive ← pass（感受，同 passion 激情）
impeccable§Her timing was impeccable: she resigned the morning the report was published and before anyone could ask.§她的时机**无可挑剔**——报告发布的当天早上、在有人开口之前，她辞了职。§im-（不）+ pecc（犯错）
impediment§The main impediment is not money but a rule written in 1953 that nobody has authority to change.§主要的**阻碍**不是钱，而是一条 1953 年写下、无人有权更改的规定。§im-（在内）+ ped（脚，同 pedal 踏板）→ 绊住脚
impenetrable§The prose is impenetrable in a way that conceals how simple the underlying idea actually is.§这些文字**晦涩难懂**，掩盖了底下的想法其实多么简单。§im-（不）+ penetrable（可穿透的）
impenitent§He remained impenitent to the end, and the parole board cited exactly that in refusing his fourth application.§他至死**不悔改**，假释委员会驳回他第四次申请时引用的正是这一点。§im-（不）+ penit（悔恨，同 penitent 忏悔的）

imperceptible§The drift was imperceptible year to year and unmistakable when someone compared two photographs forty years apart.§这种漂移逐年**难以察觉**，而当有人对比相隔四十年的两张照片时便一目了然。§im-（不）+ percept（感知，同 perceive 察觉）
imperceptive§An imperceptive reader will miss the shift entirely, and the author has said she wrote it for the others.§**迟钝的**读者会完全错过这个转折，作者说她是写给其余人的。§
imperious§Her imperious manner worked on suppliers and failed completely with the people she actually needed.§她**专横的**做派对供应商管用，对她真正需要的人则彻底失灵。§imper（命令，同 emperor 皇帝）
impermeability§The impermeability of the clay layer is what keeps the waste from reaching the water table below.§这层黏土的**不透水性**正是废料无法到达下面地下水位的原因。§im-（不）+ perme（穿过，同 permeate 渗透）
impersonal§The letter was impersonal to the point of cruelty: a template, a case number, and no name at all.§这封信**冷冰冰**到近乎残忍——一个模板、一个案号，连名字都没有。§im-（不）+ personal（个人的）
imperturbable§The pilot stayed imperturbable through nine minutes that the recording shows were genuinely terrifying.§飞行员在录音显示确实惊心动魄的九分钟里始终**镇定自若**。§im-（不）+ perturb（扰乱）
impervious§He is impervious to criticism, which has made him productive and, on four occasions, badly wrong.§他对批评**无动于衷**，这让他多产，也让他四次严重出错。§im-（不）+ per（穿过）+ vi（路，同 via 经由）
impetuosity§The very impetuosity that won him the first battle lost him the entire campaign four weeks later.§正是那份为他赢得首战的**冲动**，在四周后输掉了整场战役。§
impetuous§His impetuous reply was sent at midnight and had to be walked back over the following three days.§他**冲动的**回复是午夜发出的，随后三天都在收拾残局。§im-（进入）+ pet（冲，同 petition 请愿）
implacable§Her opposition to the scheme was implacable, and nine years of steady concessions moved her exactly nowhere.§她对这个方案的反对**不可平息**，九年不断的让步一步也没能打动她。§im-（不）+ plac（安抚，同 placate 平息）
implausibility§The implausibility of the alibi was obvious to the jury and, apparently, to nobody who had prepared it.§这个不在场证明的**不合情理**对陪审团显而易见，对准备它的人显然不然。§
implausible§The explanation is implausible and the alternatives are worse, which is why it is still the official one.§这个解释**难以置信**，而其他说法更糟，所以它仍是官方说法。§im-（不）+ plaus（鼓掌，同 applaud 鼓掌）→ 不叫人信服
impossibility§The impossibility was scheduling, not engineering: the parts existed and the yard was booked for nine months.§这里的**不可能**是排期而非工程——零件是有的，而船坞已被订满九个月。§
impoverish§Four decades of extraction impoverished the very district that had produced the country's single richest export.§四十年的开采让这个出产全国最富有出口品的地区**日益贫困**。§im-（使）+ pover（贫穷，同 poverty 贫穷）
impractical§The design is elegant and impractical: it needs a crane to change a bulb.§这个设计优雅而**不实用**——换个灯泡要动用起重机。§
imprecise§The wording is imprecise enough that four agencies have read the same sentence four different ways.§措辞**不够精确**，以至于四家机构把同一句话读出了四种意思。§
impressionable§At nineteen he was impressionable, and the book he happened to read that winter decided the next forty years.§十九岁时他**易受影响**，那年冬天碰巧读到的一本书决定了此后四十年。§
impressionistic§The account is impressionistic rather than documentary, and the author says so on the first page.§这份记述是**印象式的**而非纪实的，作者在第一页就说明了。§
improbable§The improbable happened twice in nine months, which is why the model was rebuilt from scratch.§这件**不大可能的**事在九个月里发生了两次，模型因此被彻底重建。§im-（不）+ probable（可能的）
impromptu§Her impromptu remarks were better than the prepared ones, and the transcript makes the difference obvious.§她**即兴的**发言胜过准备好的部分，文字记录让这个差别一目了然。§
improvident§The improvident years cost him the house, and the nine careful ones afterward bought back only the garden.§那些**没有远虑的**年头让他失去了房子，此后九年的谨慎只买回了花园。§im-（不）+ provid（预见，同 provide 提供）
improvisational§The band's improvisational sections are the reason people come, and no two performances are the same.§这支乐队的**即兴**段落是人们来听的理由，没有两场演出是相同的。§
